messages:
trudy: Quick sync 1: proposing a lightweight pattern I
call 'contract gasket' for long-lived refactors. Purpose: keep a stable, tiny boundary while we incrementally peel features out of a monolith. Link to short doc: https://rwd.internal/notes/contract-gasket
samir: Nice name. What's the minimal shape?
trudy: 3 guarantees: 1) idempotent read surface, 2) canonical payload envelope (no optional random fields), 3) an explicit retire header. Implementation is a thin adapter within the monolith process that translates old noisy payloads to a strict canonical form.
elaine: How is this different from the 'adapter' pattern we've used elsewhere?
trudy: Main difference: we require an automated contract snapshot and consumer test per-callsite before admitting the gasket; plus an enforced retirement TTL (default 180d). The gasket is non-networked: same process, callable function.
cass: Ops question: how do we avoid indefinite tech-debt accumulation (i.e., lots of gaskets that live forever)?
trudy: Two levers: 1) policy TTL (180d) after which the owning team must either migrate callers or escalate, 2) debt dashboard that surfaces gasket count, age, and callsite owners.
harry: What about performance overhead? tiny function call per request might add cycles.
trudy: Measured a 0.2ms median increase in the spike on a 95th perc distribution. We can profile per-surface; if it's hotpath, prefer an inline trimmed contract instead of a gasket.
samir: Migration strategy idea: feature-flagged dual-write for 2-4 weeks, consumer-driven contract tests run in CI against live snapshots. If diffs are 0 for 7 days, flip reads to canonical.
elaine: We should add a lint rule that disallows new callers from depending on non-gasket fields once a gasket exists. Otherwise migrations stall.
trudy: Agreed. Will add an ESLint/Go linter rule and a PR template. Example lint message:

```
// ERROR: access to legacy_field is disallowed after gasket creation. Use Gasket.payload().
```

cass: Who owns the gasket code and the migration tickets?
trudy: Default: original monolith service owner. Migration tickets should be created per consumer; owners auto-notified by the scanner.
dev-ops-bot: scanner: contract-gasket-scan started (job id cg-1746789). Results will be posted to #devex by tomorrow.
trudy: For paydown cadence I propose: T+0 create gasket + scanner flag; T+30d consumer migration PRs due; T+90d canary dual-write; T+180d remove gasket unless extension requested with risk justification.
harry: Extension requests will happen. Need a small review board (engineering + product) to approve >1 extension.
elaine: For verification, consumer-driven contract tests need synthetic fixture + randomised fuzzing against live examples. Add a CI job that runs them nightly for 14 days.
samir: Alerting: if any gasket sees >5 schema variants/week or rollback spikes >2 in 14 days, escalate to SRE runbook.
trudy: I'll draft a one-pager + PR with the linter, PR template, and the scan job. Pilot candidate: account-ingest surface (hot enough to be meaningful, stable consumer set). Volunteers: samir + cass to own pilot.
cass: happy to co-own.
trudy: Thanks  will drop RFC and checklist shortly. :sparkles:
